item.content:encoded:
This is not vampires. They don't suck blood because it's yummy, they eat bone marrow so they can use the stem cells to regenerate. I know there are portrays of vampires that are more brutal than just two bloody dots on the neck, and this one is even more than those. The science behind it was explained good enough that anyone can understand it. And removing the logs was a great idea, I like to think the infected as looking perfectly normal from the outside but they're screwed in the head and they'll get extremely violent if they're not fed (like they're wild beasts).

My only issue with this is the redacted/expunged data. I think it is unnecessary to black out what glands secrete the fluid that is filled with the retrovirus or how many times this is more complex than a normal virus.

+1 because of all the people who downvoted it saying ''it's just vampires explained differently''

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As a fan of vampires, and someone with less than the average disgust for the T-books (I sincerely don't mind them sparkling, and liked most of the concepts, but it is still very badly written at the end of the day), I still have to agree that Virus-pires aren't a novel idea at all.

+ My opinion on how to improve it
- But that is besides the point

That is the main mistake in this skip, since the beginning: it puts too much effort in simply being yet-again-another-explanation-for-vampires, without adding anything else. Well, as much as a sci-fi take on things is more to the taste of many readers here, the Foundation does find anomalies that can't be explained without magic for now, so it could very well be cursed-by-god-vampires without changing nothing. Of course, would still remain doing nothing.

My suggestion, if this ever come to be re-written again, is to actually do something unexpected with the viral twist. Add something either to its properties or the story that really exists solely because this thing is a virus, not a curse. There are plenty of good skips doing this: the thing is extremely similar to the legend, but removed from its original context it shows something. Like 166, that is a succubus trying to live the life of a normal nun, with a lot of seductive powers turned into annoying medical conditions.

- But that is besides the point

But there are also two other problems that are more urgent in actually keeping it from being at least an entertaining read. Too much expungements that aren't needed, and the bit about subservience at the bottom. Those bits aren't needed and seem forced on an otherwise well written article.

item.content:encoded:
Bad expungements. Scattered spottiness in the writing that could be easily edited. Oh, and…

Instances of SCP-742-1 behave subserviently toward the instance that infected them.

Still vampires. Still please no. Virus-pires are not new, and this remaining blatant vampire ripoff just makes an otherwise potentially interesting supernatural being into 'just another vampire ripoff', just like a certain book-turned-movie-series I'm sure we all want to never see the sun again.

EDIT: Y'know, looking back at it, this also really doesn't feel like it belongs as a Keter. Not especially hard or complicated to contain, or super likely to go into a huge self-replicating spree given the text as read. Euclid is plenty for this.

item.title: Ow.
item.content:encoded:
Okay. I liked this. Halfway through, I upvoted, because the concept is cool and to a layman like myself the sciencebabble is beievable and not overpowering. A few sections, specifically throwaway lines about treatment of foetuses and "undesireable recessive genes" were excellent.

Then…

I got to the logs.

The logs there take a really sweet pod people-esque "they are dangerous and walk among us" vibe with a viable hook and turn it into a cliche ridden Underground Vampyre Societie meets the morrowind beholder's cult thing that is meh in the extreme. Everything from the narmy "oh, it must be safe here AAAAAAGH" beginning section to the exceedingly predictable "Oh, I thought you were dead. Oh well, welcome back AAAAAAAGH" ending screamed dissapointing, and the line about "the master" actually made me facepalm.

That's right, alias. I facepalmed, in real life. I wasn't ready for it, and I knocked my glasses off, and it hurt, and it's all your fault. Feel bad.

But seriously, the concept here is good, and the description is excellent. Everything but the logs is great and upvote worthy. I reccomend you heavily rewrite or just remove the loggy transcript bits, because then I will upvote this and perhaps manage not to bruise my own forehead next time I read it.
